name: Starting Shelf Island

views.label: Detail 5: The door and its rock pillars
Detail 10: Rock pillars on the cliff

desc: a floating shelf of dark rock 40 m wide and 56 m long with a ragged asymmetric outline, about 6 m thick at the rim and tapering into an inverted cone 48 m deep with a faint bronze vein glowing inside it, six thick rusted chains hanging from bronze rim rings into the haze. At the near end is the SPAWN TERRACE, an irregular paved patch about 13 x 9 m of cracked slabs of different sizes, with a shallow bronze arrival disc (3.6 m across, three concentric rings, slightly sunken and cracked) at its centre and a low broken rock lip behind it; a tiny plain 1.8 m human silhouette stands on the disc facing the door in every view for scale. A broken road of uneven worn slabs about 4 m wide, with a thin broken bronze inlay line, leads about 11 m to THE BEAM: one colossal weathered bronze I-girder 16 m long with a 2.5 m wide top, lying slightly crooked (about 15 degrees off the straight line) across a ragged meandering crack that cuts the whole island from rim to rim, 8 to 11 m wide with stepped broken lips and a 60 m drop into haze; the beam is level but dented, rust-streaked, matte, dusty, with missing rivets and a chipped corner, never polished. Beyond it a broken irregular forecourt about 13 x 4 m, then three worn uneven steps rising to THE DOOR, shown LOCKED, cut into the face of a huge black rock cliff with raw rock on both sides: 8 m high, carved stone frame 7.6 m wide with a crown of bronze finials, battered green-bronze verdigris scrollwork leaves dark with soot, two thick rusted chains wound across both leaves held by one huge closed padlock, a thin bright amber line of light through the centre gap, exactly like the Core Fantasy key-art door. Behind the door the cliff holds a walkable antechamber: a 3 m passage, then an irregular carved hall about 16 x 11.5 m with an 11 m cracked ceiling, four stout columns (two whole, two broken) around a clear aisle, a low round dais 4.5 m across where three weapons hover, completely dark inside with no daylight (only the faint glow of the weapons), a small west alcove, and, at the east side of the hall, a short flight of 5 wide worn stone steps going DOWN into a 4 m opening (the exit tunnel) in the east wall that leads out onto a rock ledge on the cliffs east face where a fixed bridge leaves toward the next island. The door sits low at the foot of ONE enormous, deep, solid mountain of black-brown fractured rock that rises 36 m at its west shoulder and 60 m at its summit, as thick and heavy as it is tall, with a huge cave carved inside it. The whole mass is built from countless big rough boulders, slabs, ribs and buttresses piled and jammed together, so the area around the door is crowded with many large rocks and ledges, with broken scree at their feet. Its upper part splits into two high crooked peaks (60 m and a 36 m one leaning west), which are simply the top of the same mass, not separate objects. All one rock: NO windows, NO openings, NO bricks or cut stone, NO tiers, NO battlements, NO carvings, nothing built. Only a faint amber glow deep in a few natural cracks. Around the base stand six chunky broken rock outcrops of 20 to 48 m, different heights, thick at the base, blunt snapped tops, NOT needles, NOT cones, NOT icicles. NO masonry on them: no bricks or courses of cut stone, no battlements, no crenellations, no arched windows, no columns, no domes, no bands or carved panels, nothing that looks built, Roman or medieval. Three bare dead trees (6 m, 4.5 m, and a 2.8 m broken stump) stand off the road, a few small uneven clumps of dry grass, and rubble in uneven scatters of different-sized stones; no mirror symmetry anywhere, immense, silent and ominous; match the attached approved ENV-01 hero image and blueprint sheets exactly, and add no second floating island or extra rock in the background

One weathered bronze ring band, dented and green with verdigris, is wrapped around its waist. On the flat top, on the west edge, a short fixed stone bridge arrives and ends at a small bronze anchor socket set in the rock; on the east edge, a thin plank-and-chain bridge leaves from a second small bronze anchor socket. One thick rusted chain hangs from a bronze rim ring on the pad edge into the haze. One bare dead tree and a few small clumps of dry grass grow on the top. The top is cracked slabs of different sizes with loose chips. Everything is natural rock except the two bridge ends, the two anchor sockets, the chain and the bronze ring. Rough, grimy and uneven, never smooth, never tidy. No buildings, no walls, no windows, no arches

name: Medium Island with Windbreak
desc: a medium floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 30 m wide, with a ragged uneven outline and a heavy rough underside. Along its north edge rises ONE GRAND MASSIF of natural rock: huge, thick and monumental, like a small mountain range or the great rock buttes of a canyon land, and like the tall rock clusters in the approved key art. It is a single mass that grows out of the island with no gaps at its base. It has a very wide heavy base about 22 m wide, and out of it rise five or six enormous crags of very different heights. TOWERING is the point. The crags are like the great spires of the Dolomites, the basalt pillars of Zhangjiajie and the fractured slate peaks of a mountain range, only crooked and leaning. THE BIGGEST CRAG RISES ABOUT TWICE AS HIGH AS THE WHOLE ISLAND IS WIDE (about 55 m on a 30 m island), so in the front view it is far taller than the island is long, and the island looks small beneath it. The second crag is about 38 m, then 34 m, 26 m, 18 m and 12 m, so the skyline is a jagged crown of very different heights: one extra tall spire, two or three tall ones, then medium ones and low broken shoulders. Do NOT make them all the same height. Every crag is thick at the base and rises in a long tapering shape, narrowing unevenly toward a ragged broken top, with long vertical fluting and deep vertical cracks, big ledges, overhangs and collapsed notches, wind grooves and thin lighter brown seams. They stand as ONE TIGHT OVERLAPPING CLUSTER, NOT in a fan, NOT in a row, NOT side by side like the fingers of a hand: some crags in front, some behind, two leaning against each other, one leaning out over the hollow, each leaning 10 to 25 degrees at a different angle, tops broken and jagged, the tallest off to the left of centre. They are fused at the base into one wide heavy mass with lower rock buttresses and stepped shoulders, with a few fallen boulders at the foot. They are NOT short blunt boulders, NOT squat blocks, NOT thin slabs, NOT planks, NOT fins, NOT ribs, NOT teeth, NOT stacked blocks, NOT toy bricks, NOT a neat row of equal stones, NOT like fingers, and NOT icicles or cones. In front of the crags the top dips into a small sheltered hollow with a plain flat floor of bare dark rock with nothing lying on it, thin straight bronze lines inlaid in the floor leading to one short stone column on a round bronze base with a small dark fire bowl on top, unlit. There are no steps, no stairs and no platforms. On the west edge a thin plank-and-chain bridge arrives at a short bronze socket post, and on the east edge a short fixed stone bridge end with a second short bronze socket post leaves toward the next place. The posts are plain short bronze posts. The underside tapers to a rough cone with a few long hanging rock tendrils and a faint bronze vein deep in the cracks. At the south-east edge, away from the crags, a big flat-topped natural boulder with a worn smooth top sits right on the rim, facing the open sky. Nobody sits on it. NOTHING ELSE: no props, no loose slabs, no extra bowls, no grass, no stumps, no rubble on the floor, no moss. It is dry and dead. Rough, grimy and uneven, never smooth, never tidy. Nothing is built: no buildings, no walls, no windows, no arches, no stairs
short: A crooked crest of tall and extra tall rock spires shelters a quiet hollow with the first ignition column

name: Large Plateau Island
desc: a large floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 60 m wide, with sheer broken cliff faces all around, a ragged oval outline, and a deep underside like an upside-down mountain of fractured rock with a few long hanging rock tendrils and a faint bronze vein deep in the cracks. In the middle of the top is one DEEP CRATER, about 30 m across and 18 m deep, with sheer cracked rock walls and three broad broken ledges stepping down to a flat floor far below. The crater is an irregular oval, NOT round, NOT neat rings, NOT a stadium, NOT a quarry with tidy steps. Thin amber light glows faintly in the cracks of the crater floor and walls, dim and dormant, like a sleeping reservoir of energy. Thin straight bronze lines are inlaid in the crater floor. Around the crater rim stand six huge NATURAL ROCK SPIRES of very different heights, scattered at different distances, some close together in pairs and some alone, NOT in a row, NOT in a fan, NOT like fingers. The two biggest stand at the east edge and lean toward each other with a narrow gap about 6 m wide between them, like a natural rock gate: the tallest is about as tall as the whole island is wide (about 55 m), the other about 44 m. The four others, along the north and south-east rims, are about 34 m, 28 m, 22 m and 16 m. Every spire is thick at the base, tapering, crooked, ragged, with deep vertical cracks, ledges and broken tops, each leaning at a different angle. They are like the giant natural rock spires in the approved key art, very grand, the island looks small beneath the tallest. They are NOT thin slabs, NOT fins, NOT teeth, NOT stacked blocks, NOT toy bricks, NOT icicles or cones. At the west edge is a flat landing about 10 m wide with a low natural rock lip. From the landing three rough broken rock paths lead east: one along the north rim, one along the south rim, and one straight out toward the crater edge. On the east rim of the crater, near the gate, stands ONE short stone column on a round bronze base with a small dark fire bowl on top, unlit. There is exactly ONE column, no second one. Through the gap between the two big spires a short fixed stone bridge end with one short bronze socket post leaves toward the next place. NOTHING ELSE: no props, no loose slabs, no floating slabs, no extra bowls, no grass, no trees, no stumps, no moss. It is dry and dead. Rough, grimy and uneven, never smooth, never tidy. Nothing is built: no buildings, no walls, no windows, no arches, no stairs, no tall structures of any kind
short: A deep glowing crater ringed by giant natural rock spires, three ways across, one ignition column and a natural rock gate

name: Long Causeway Island
desc: a very long, narrow, THIN floating island of the same dark black-brown fractured boulder rock as the Starting Shelf Island, about 80 m long and only 10 m wide, about EIGHT TIMES AS LONG AS IT IS WIDE, like a long flat blade or a fallen mountain ridge. It is a thin slab, only about 8 m thick in the middle, tapering to a point at both ends, with sheer broken cliff sides and a shallow underside with a few long hanging rock tendrils at the east end. The west end is where the player arrives and the east end is where he leaves. The top is a clean, open, flat-ish back of cracked dark rock, about 10 m wide, rough and uneven, with sheer drops on both sides. You can see right along it from end to end. One thin, perfectly straight bronze line is inlaid down the exact middle of the top, running the whole length. Along both edges of the back stand HUGE NATURAL ROCK SPIRES, thick at the base, tapering, crooked, ragged, with sharp angular fractured faces, long vertical cracks and broken tops, exactly like the giant natural rock spires of the approved key art and like the two gate spires of the Large Plateau Island. They stand in leaning PAIRS, one on the north edge and one on the south edge, leaning toward each other ACROSS the walking back so that their tops almost touch, like the natural rock gate on the Large Plateau Island. In a row from west to east: a small pair about 16 m high near the west end; a bigger pair about 24 m high close beside it; then a long open gap; then a broken pair in the middle where the south spire stands about 20 m high and its partner on the north edge has snapped off to a jagged stump about 5 m high; then the TALLEST pair just east of the middle, about 34 m high (the tallest reaches almost half as high as the island is long) with a narrow gap of about 4 m between their tops; then one single low spire about 9 m high on the north edge near the east end. The heights are very different and the spacing is uneven. At the west end a short flat tongue of the same rock, with one short bronze post at its tip, reaches out toward the previous island, and at the east end a second short flat tongue of rock with one short bronze post reaches out toward the next place. NOTHING ELSE: no props, no loose slabs, no boulders or rubble lying on the back, no grass, no trees, no stumps, no moss. It is dry and dead. Rough, grimy and uneven, never smooth, never tidy. Nothing is built: no buildings, no walls, no windows, no stairs, no towers
short: A very long thin rock blade with pairs of giant natural spires leaning together across the path

desc: a tall rock spire tilted at a dramatic angle as if caught mid-fall, held up by one thick natural rock buttress of the same stone, the upper block cracked through and about to snap, tense and mysterious. Natural dark black-brown fractured rock only, in the same rock as the ENV-01 hero: sharp angular faces, horizontal strata, long vertical cracks, grime and wear. NO masonry, no bricks, no battlements, no arched windows, no carved panels, no gold or bronze bands, no buttress arches, no doors, no stairs, nothing built by people. Only thin faint amber light inside a few deep cracks.
short: Rock spire tilted mid-fall

name: Needle Rock Spire
desc: an impossibly slender needle of dark natural rock, tapering to a razor-sharp point, fractured strata along its whole height, standing alone on a small rough base, awe-inspiring. Natural dark black-brown fractured rock only, in the same rock as the ENV-01 hero: sharp angular faces, horizontal strata, long vertical cracks, grime and wear. NO masonry, no bricks, no battlements, no arched windows, no carved panels, no gold or bronze bands, no buttress arches, no doors, no stairs, nothing built by people. Only thin faint amber light inside a few deep cracks.
short: Impossibly slender 45 m needle spire

name: Twin Rock Spires
desc: two huge natural rock spires of different heights standing side by side on one shared rough base, one with a cracked broken top and one with a sharp point, a deep gap between them, no bridge and no arch, grand and silent. Natural dark black-brown fractured rock only, in the same rock as the ENV-01 hero: sharp angular faces, horizontal strata, long vertical cracks, grime and wear. NO masonry, no bricks, no battlements, no arched windows, no carved panels, no gold or bronze bands, no buttress arches, no doors, no stairs, nothing built by people. Only thin faint amber light inside a few deep cracks.
short: Twin rock spires

name: Gate Spire Pair
desc: two huge natural rock spires leaning together so their tops almost meet, leaving a tall narrow dark passage between them at the base, like a natural gate, rough strata and fallen rubble at their feet. Natural dark black-brown fractured rock only, in the same rock as the ENV-01 hero: sharp angular faces, horizontal strata, long vertical cracks, grime and wear. NO masonry, no bricks, no battlements, no arched windows, no carved panels, no gold or bronze bands, no buttress arches, no doors, no stairs, nothing built by people. Only thin faint amber light inside a few deep cracks.
short: Two spires leaning into a gate

name: Long Rung Bridge
desc: a very long bridge made of two heavy dark chains with flat rungs, sagging slightly, anchored with bronze posts on a flat rock tongue at both ends, only the first four rungs at the near end glow amber-white and the rest are dark, the same make as the other canyon bridges, as in the Leap key art; fixed and rigid, not swaying
short: Long chain-and-rung bridge, first four rungs glowing

name: Leech Bridge Underside
size: 20 to 72 m long, fits the bridge
desc: the same long plank-and-chain bridge seen from slightly below, with four armored Ember Leeches clinging upside down to the underside planks and chains in the shadow, their tail sacs glowing a dull ember, one stretching up toward the walkway; dark, tense, mysterious
short: Leeches hanging under the bridge

name: Six-Line Floor Inlay
desc: a round paving plaza of cracked dark stone with six parallel straight bronze inlay bars set into the floor, glowing faintly amber, each bar a different length-matched element texture; shown dormant and lit
short: Six glowing bars inlaid in the floor

name: Fire Brazier, Standing
desc: a wide shallow bronze bowl on a short flared bronze stand sitting on the ground, burning with a steady lively flame and a few rising sparks, as the lone brazier in the Igara key art; weathered, ancient and simple
short: Standing bronze fire bowl

name: Great Leaning Rock Spire
desc: a very grand leaning spire of dark natural rock about 80 m tall, in rough stacked tiers, with smaller jagged rock spires clinging to its flanks, deep cracks, wind-worn, dramatic and ominous. Natural dark black-brown fractured rock only, in the same rock as the ENV-01 hero: sharp angular faces, horizontal strata, long vertical cracks, grime and wear. NO masonry, no bricks, no battlements, no arched windows, no carved panels, no gold or bronze bands, no buttress arches, no doors, no stairs, nothing built by people. Only thin faint amber light inside a few deep cracks.
short: Grand leaning rock spire

name: Obsidian Shard Cluster
desc: a leaning cluster of huge black obsidian blades with glassy edges and amber reflections, rising from tan rock, as the shard formations in the Igara key art
short: Leaning obsidian blade cluster

name: Dead Tree Grove
desc: a small group of three bare petrified dead trees with twisting branches and splintered roots gripping a rock slab, as in the Igara key art
short: Three dead trees on a rock slab

name: Bronze Door, Unlocked
desc: the same tall ornate double door in its carved stone frame with bronze finials and battered verdigris scrollwork panels, now UNLOCKED: the huge padlock hangs open and the thick rusted chains have slid off and lie in heavy coils on the cracked paving, the two leaves still shut but a little loose, a brighter thin vertical amber light between them
short: The same tall ornate double door in its carved stone frame

name: Bronze Door, Open
desc: the same tall ornate double door in its carved stone frame with bronze finials, now OPEN: both battered verdigris leaves swung inward, the broken chains and open padlock lying on the paving, a deep stone antechamber beyond lit by warm gold-amber light pouring out across the floor, dust motes in the beams
short: The same tall ornate double door in its carved stone frame

name: Dark Ore Seal
desc: a crust of dark volcanic ore, black and glassy with thin dull-gold veins, growing over and sealing a small object like a hard shell, rough lumpy surface, a few faint amber cracks showing warmth underneath; shown SEALED and whole (and a second version after burning: the ore cracked open and glowing red at the edges, breaking away in chunks with sparks and smoke)
short: A crust of dark volcanic ore

name: Memory Chest
desc: a small old chest of dark stone bound with aged bronze straps, a rounded lid, worn corners and soot, one thin gold line of light along the seam of the lid; it sits half sunk in rock rubble under a cap of dark ore (shown SEALED), and a second version OPEN: the lid up and a soft warm gold light and a few drifting sparks rising out of it; no skulls, no gems, no jewels, no gold coins
short: A small old chest of dark stone bound

name: Wind Vent Wall
desc: a round vent mouth about 1.5 m across set into a sheer wall of dark fractured rock, a heavy rim of weathered bronze around it, a visible stream of pale gold wind with swirling dust pouring out of it upward; a short rock ledge above it that the wind lifts a person toward; shown IDLE (a faint dusty breath only) and a second version BLOWING (a strong gold column of wind with sparks)
short: A round vent mouth about 1.5 m across set into a sheer wall of dark fractured ro

name: Leech Nest
desc: a heap of Ember Leech egg-sacs and shed shells clinging to the rock and the underside of a bridge, glossy dark black-brown, translucent amber sacs with a faint orange glow inside, a few young leeches half out of the sacs and curled legs, a slick trail of dark resin; crawling and unpleasant, not gory
short: A heap of Ember Leech egg-sacs and shed shells clinging to the rock and the unde

name: Six-Line Ladder, Dormant
desc: six very large straight horizontal beams of dark bronze with small end caps, stacked vertically with even spacing, parallel and equal in length, floating in the sky; shown dormant and unlit, each beam the size of a bridge; flat straight bars only, not a star shape, not a circle
short: Six very large straight horizontal beams of dark bronze

name: Six-Line Ladder, Progress States
desc: six equal straight horizontal glowing bars stacked vertically like the Interface key art, hot amber-white core, soft amber glow haze and a few embers drifting around them; show three versions side by side: bottom bar lit, bottom four lit, all six lit; unlit bars dark bronze; flat straight bars only
short: Six equal straight horizontal glowing bars stacked vertically like the Interface

name: Fire Eye, Open and Burning
desc: the Fire Eye, copy the attached Fire Eye key art exactly (same eye in all four Fire Eye states, only the state changes): one huge almond-shaped eye seen as a living organ, the whole eye built from fine fibers: a thick eyelid rim of braided, twisting glowing fibers like muscle and fire threads, NO smooth white sclera and NO smooth polished rim; a wide iris ring of fine radial fibers like a sun, white-gold at its inner edge and amber-orange outward; a TALL NARROW vertical pupil like a long pointed slit or leaf, almost black with a dark red edge (not a small diamond); long thin jagged flame filaments and lightning-like tendrils streaming outward from the whole outline like a solar corona; ORGANIC, NOT METAL: no steel, no plates, no stone carving, no engraving, no twigs or thorn lashes; eye only, no face, no body. STATE: OPEN and burning, full bright fire, white-gold lid rim, orange-amber iris, full corona of flame filaments.
short: The Fire Eye, open and burning

name: Ringed Planet
desc: a very large ringed planet filling a big part of the sky, warm sepia and tan cloud bands, a thin pale ring crossing in front, bright rim halo on the sun side, as in the Fire Dragon and Interface key art
short: A very large ringed planet filling a big part of the sky

name: Plain Planet
desc: a large cratered brown-amber planet with a dark terminator shadow, no rings, soft rim glow, visible surface texture, as in the Fire Dragon key art
short: A large cratered brown-amber planet

name: Ember Planet
desc: a large dark planet cracked with glowing molten-orange fault lines like a cooling coal, a thin atmosphere halo of amber haze on one edge, no rings, hangs low on the horizon
short: Cracked molten ember planet

name: Fire Eye, Open and Dormant
desc: the Fire Eye, copy the attached Fire Eye key art exactly (same eye in all four Fire Eye states, only the state changes): one huge almond-shaped eye seen as a living organ, the whole eye built from fine fibers: a thick eyelid rim of braided, twisting glowing fibers like muscle and fire threads, NO smooth white sclera and NO smooth polished rim; a wide iris ring of fine radial fibers like a sun, white-gold at its inner edge and amber-orange outward; a TALL NARROW vertical pupil like a long pointed slit or leaf, almost black with a dark red edge (not a small diamond); long thin jagged flame filaments and lightning-like tendrils streaming outward from the whole outline like a solar corona; ORGANIC, NOT METAL: no steel, no plates, no stone carving, no engraving, no twigs or thorn lashes; eye only, no face, no body. STATE: OPEN and dormant, fire out. The same fibers are now cold: dark charred brown-black fibrous lid rim, the iris ring of fine radial fibers dull dark ember-brown, only a faint ember glow deep in the tall slit pupil, the outline filaments short, dead, ashy and sooty instead of flame; same shape and proportions.
short: Open Eye, fire out

name: Fire Eye, Closed and Burning
desc: the Fire Eye, copy the attached Fire Eye key art exactly (same eye in all four Fire Eye states, only the state changes): one huge almond-shaped eye seen as a living organ, the whole eye built from fine fibers: a thick eyelid rim of braided, twisting glowing fibers like muscle and fire threads, NO smooth white sclera and NO smooth polished rim; a wide iris ring of fine radial fibers like a sun, white-gold at its inner edge and amber-orange outward; a TALL NARROW vertical pupil like a long pointed slit or leaf, almost black with a dark red edge (not a small diamond); long thin jagged flame filaments and lightning-like tendrils streaming outward from the whole outline like a solar corona; ORGANIC, NOT METAL: no steel, no plates, no stone carving, no engraving, no twigs or thorn lashes; eye only, no face, no body. STATE: CLOSED and burning. The two lids are sealed along one single bright white-gold seam, the lid surface is the same fibrous braided glowing orange, no iris and no pupil visible, the flame filaments and tendrils still streaming from the outline.
short: Closed Eye, burning

name: Fire Eye, Closed and Dormant
desc: the Fire Eye, copy the attached Fire Eye key art exactly (same eye in all four Fire Eye states, only the state changes): one huge almond-shaped eye seen as a living organ, the whole eye built from fine fibers: a thick eyelid rim of braided, twisting glowing fibers like muscle and fire threads, NO smooth white sclera and NO smooth polished rim; a wide iris ring of fine radial fibers like a sun, white-gold at its inner edge and amber-orange outward; a TALL NARROW vertical pupil like a long pointed slit or leaf, almost black with a dark red edge (not a small diamond); long thin jagged flame filaments and lightning-like tendrils streaming outward from the whole outline like a solar corona; ORGANIC, NOT METAL: no steel, no plates, no stone carving, no engraving, no twigs or thorn lashes; eye only, no face, no body. STATE: CLOSED and dormant, fire out. The lids are sealed along one single dark seam with a faint dull ember glow hidden inside it, the lid surface the same braided fibrous texture but cold, dark charred brown-black like burnt muscle and ash crust, a few short dead ashy filaments at the corners; same shape and proportions.
short: Closed Eye, fire out

name: Six Lines, Six Elements (proposed)
desc: six equal straight horizontal bars stacked vertically with even spacing, each bar a different element yet the same size: bar one glowing embers and coal, bar two molten bronze, bar three spiralling wind and dust streaks, bar four crackling lightning, bar five flowing liquid fire, bar six pure white-gold light; all six clearly straight bars, all in the warm gold-amber palette
short: Six lines as six elements

name: The Throne of Stillness
desc: a colossal ancient throne hewn from black volcanic stone and aged bronze, about 40 m tall, unmistakably a throne: a deep massive seat block with two thick armrests, and rising far above it a very tall narrow monolith backrest with straight parallel sides and a flat top with ONE small rectangular notch in the middle, EXACTLY SIX short horizontal glowing amber bars (fissures) stacked at equal spacing up the front face of the backrest like a ladder of fire (count them: six), hot molten-amber cracks veining through the lower backrest and the stone like lava under a crust, on EACH side a cluster of THREE colossal curved tapering bronze ribs like dragon ribs or tusks (three on the left, three on the right, six in all) rising from the rock base and arching inward over the seat without touching, with molten fire glowing between them at their base, a short steep stair of broken black stone up the front to the seat with two small bronze braziers burning at the top corners and two at the foot of the stair, a rough broken rock plinth under everything, heavy rough weathered surfaces, thin embers rising
short: A colossal ancient throne hewn from black volcanic stone and aged bronze

name: The Cinder (guide)
desc: a small floating faceted polyhedron fire construct about the size of a head, gold-bronze angular frame with glass-like triangular and hexagonal facets around a bright glowing ember core with a faint engraved symbol, no face, no limbs; shown LIT with a warm halo and a few drifting sparks (a second version DIM: core nearly out, frame cold, as in the Cinder key art)
short: A small floating faceted polyhedron fire construct about the size of a head

name: Fire Dragon
desc: a MASSIVE winged fire dragon matching the Fire Dragon key art: dark scaled body cracked with glowing amber-ember seams, huge membrane wings with ember-lit veins, spiked head ridge, long neck, jaws open breathing a long roaring stream of orange fire with sparks, long body and tail, shown flying; large enough to carry a rider on its shoulders
short: A MASSIVE winged fire dragon matching the Fire Dragon key art: dark scaled body

name: Glass Shadow
desc: a tall humanoid figure of CLEAR TRANSPARENT glass crystal with a light amber-gold tint, matching the attached Glass Shadows key art exactly: you can see through the body and see inner facets and fine crossing crack lines, mirror-like reflections on the faceted chest and shoulders, a smooth faceless faceted head, slim athletic build, small glowing gold shards breaking off one arm with a spray of tiny sparks, a faint warm core glow inside the chest, NOT opaque, NOT solid orange or gold metal, NOT a statue, symbolic force not a person
short: A tall humanoid figure of CLEAR TRANSPARENT glass crystal

name: Rock Mage
desc: a Rock Mage, a hulking 3.2 m stone titan, a whole species of them, built of huge dark charcoal-black boulders in the same dark weathered rock as the islands: enormous rounded boulder shoulders, massive layered-rock arms ending in giant clenched rock fists, thick heavy pillar legs, a small rock head with no eyes, only a glowing orange-amber crack for a face and a jagged glowing mouth-crack; a web of glowing molten orange-amber cracks runs through the black rock across the chest, arms and legs, brightest at the neck and shoulders; a ring of seven or eight small rocks orbits its body at chest height; one huge glowing-amber boulder is lifted overhead in its right hand; the body is heavy, grounded and brutal like a walking cliff, never plate armour, never a knight, never a statue, never a person in a costume, symbolic force, powerful and a little absurd
short: A Rock Mage

name: Ember Leech
desc: a long armored arthropod, half giant centipede and half scorpion, matching the attached Ember Leech reference exactly: a long low body of about fourteen overlapping smooth rounded dome-shaped plates in dark glossy black-brown chitin with worn bronze-brown highlights along each plate edge, like polished beetle shell, getting slightly narrower toward the head; on each segment a pair of thin spindly spiked legs in dull red-brown with tiny glowing orange ember glints at the joints, gripping the stone; a small head with long thin curved mandibles; the rear end curls up and over like a scorpion tail ending in a bulging swollen sac glowing bright molten orange-yellow like lava with visible swirling heat inside, with sharp curved dark hooked pincers at its tip and a few sparks dripping from it; the glow is only at the rear sac, the leg joints and faint ember seams between plates; no wings, no eyes glowing white, no slime, no tentacles, not a worm, shown standing on a flat stone surface
short: A long armored arthropod

name: Storm Wraith (VFX reference)
desc: a large humanoid figure formed of dark swirling dust and storm cloud exactly as in the Storm Wraiths key art, long clawed hands, amber lightning veins running through it, flecks of fire in the swirl, no solid face, shown mid-stride
short: A large humanoid figure formed of dark swirling dust and storm cloud exactly as

name: Sleeping Giant Shadow
desc: a colossal sleeping giant the size of an island, lying curled on its side like a mountain range, made of black volcanic stone plates stacked like armor and drifting dust, a huge faceless rounded head resting on one arm, broad ridged back plates that a person could climb like steps, thin amber light glowing in the seams between the plates, a slow breathing chest, loose dust and small rocks drifting off it; calm and sad, not monstrous, no eyes, no mouth, no teeth; shown ASLEEP and a second version CALMED: the seams filled with warm gold light and the edges dissolving into drifting dark specks that become flying birds
short: A colossal sleeping giant the size of an island

name: Elias Cloak, Growth Stages
desc: Elias, a 21-year-old man, lean and athletic, short dark hair, a calm composed face, in his matte obsidian-black technical bodysuit with fine bronze seam-lines, shown as SIX figures standing in a row on a plain backdrop with the same pose, left to right showing how his cloak grows as he finds light: 1 no cloak, only a short frayed dark grey ash-cloth scarf; 2 a longer scarf to the waist with one thin gold edge line; 3 a short cloak to the hips with two gold edge lines; 4 a cloak to the knees with gold edge lines that glow softly; 5 a long cloak to the ankles, gold edge lines glowing and tiny embers lifting from the hem; 6 a very long flowing cloak that trails behind him, rich gold glow along every edge and the hem breaking into soft sparks; the cloth is matte, heavy, worn and dark, never shiny, never silk
short: Elias

name: Wise Turtle
desc: an enormous ancient turtle, sitting on a warm flat rock in the sun with its back to the viewer, the shell patterned with six clean horizontal lines in dark and gold like a ladder, weathered skin like old leather, small calm wise eyes, slow and still; it never speaks; a story animal, gentle and dignified
short: An enormous ancient turtle

name: Igara Birds
desc: a flock of Igara birds, medium-sized birds with dark brown backs and amber-gold underwings and long forked tails, shown in several poses: gliding, banking, perched on a rock, taking off; also a small cluster showing a flock streaming in a wide curve; graceful and plentiful
short: A flock of Igara birds

name: Elias Suit Glow
desc: a rear three-quarter view of Elias, 21, short dark hair, matte obsidian bodysuit, whose circuit seams glow bright orange-amber, a soft aura of warm light and drifting embers around his whole body; shown at low glow and at full glow
short: Orange suit seams and aura

name: Sacred Arc
desc: a wide arc of golden fire and light sweeping through the air around Elias, thick glowing flame ribbon with a hot white-gold core and trailing sparks, as in the Sacred Arc key art
short: Golden fire arc

name: Stillness Rings
desc: concentric rings of orange light expanding from Elias standing still on the ground, thin hot circles with fine ember dust lifting inside them, calm and powerful, as in the Stillness Wins key art
short: Expanding stillness rings

name: Run Sparks
desc: a trail of fire sparks and ember streaks kicked up behind Elias as he runs, small bright points streaming back along his path, as in the Flow Over Force key art
short: Sparks kicked up while running

name: Ambient Ember Sparks
desc: slow floating fire sparks and glowing embers drifting upward in warm dusty air, varied sizes, some larger glowing flakes, used around Elias and across the islands
short: Drifting embers

name: Combat Flame Ring
desc: a controlled ring of orange flame circling Elias's feet on the rock floor, low flames rising to knee height, a bright thin hot core with soft licking tongues of fire, restraint not chaos, as in the Combat Restraint key art
short: Ring of flame at his feet

name: Hidden-System Energy Orbs
desc: floating glowing orbs of amber light connected by thin bright energy threads in a loose lattice, some orbs bright and some dim, as in the Hidden System key art
short: Orbs joined by energy threads

name: Dragon Fire Breath
desc: a long roaring jet of orange fire with a white-gold core streaming from a dragon jaw outline, swirling smoke and embers, hot and powerful
short: Fire stream from the dragon

name: Ring of Fire, Dormant and Ignited
desc: a GIGANTIC ring of fire that surrounds the ENTIRE floating realm, NOT a small ring on the ground: the whole archipelago of floating rock islands, the bridges and the Throne summit all sit INSIDE the ring, which hangs in open sky at the far edge of the world, kilometers wide, seen from the Throne as a thin glowing circle on the horizon all around. It is one flat horizontal circle in the sky at the height of the islands, hanging in mid-air with no ground, no wall, no supports and no structure under it, nothing touches it. DORMANT: a very thin dark ring of cold dull ember coals and faint smoke, barely visible against the amber sky, only a few dim ember points. IGNITED (it lights up when Elias reaches the Throne at the end of the game): the whole ring bursts into a towering wall of fire with leaping flames and sparks all the way around the world, lighting the undersides of the clouds and the islands from outside
short: World-edge ring, dormant and lit

name: Cinder Throw and Recall
desc: the Cinder, a small faceted gold-bronze ember construct, thrown in a long arc across the dark leaving a thin bright gold-white trail with falling sparks; it strikes a stone surface in a burst of orange sparks, then a thin glowing thread of light pulls it back through the air into a raised open hand
short: The Cinder

name: Perfect Dodge into Calm
desc: a pale gold shockwave ring rippling out through the air at the instant of a perfect dodge, the world slowing: sparks and dust hang motionless in the air, Elias in his locked costume (matte black bodysuit with fine gold seam lines, scarf at the neck, dark cape) twisting clear of the blow, and behind him a faint ghost afterimage of a Rock Mage's huge boulder fist frozen mid-swing (the only enemy in the picture: no axes, no blades, no human weapons, no human warriors), the colors cooling and softening around the ring
short: A pale gold shockwave ring rippling out through the air at the instant of a perf

name: Enemy Tell Flashes
desc: four small warning flashes shown across the panels, each a brief bright cue just before an enemy attacks: the glowing amber crack that is a Rock Mage's face flaring bright while its ring of orbiting rocks snaps tight, a thin white glint running along the clear glass arm of a Glass Shadow, a swollen molten sac brightening at the tip of an Ember Leech's curled tail, the hot red eyes of a Bat-Bird flaring as its leathery wings snap open (only enemies that exist in this game: no armored knights, no helmets, no visors); clear, readable and brief, never a text or an arrow
short: Four small warning flashes shown across the panels

name: Mother's Whisper
desc: a small glowing ember pulsing warm rose-gold, soft slow ripples of warm light spreading from it through dusty air, the air around it dimming and going quiet, a few drifting motes of soft light rising like breath; gentle and intimate, no face, no figure, no words
short: A small glowing ember pulsing warm rose-gold

name: The Moving Calm
desc: a large soft circle of pale gold light drifting across a cracked dark stone floor, inside it the air clear and still with a few slow motes, outside it swirling storm dust and a floor of burning orange cracks; the edge of the circle is a thin glowing line with a faint haze, easy to read
short: A large soft circle of pale gold light drifting across a cracked dark stone floo

name: Memory Reveal
desc: a ghostly translucent memory scene projected into the air by a small ember, in faded warm gold sepia: a window, two silhouettes and a small boy seen from behind, with no clear faces, its edges breaking into drifting sparks and dissolving into dark air; delicate, dreamlike, slightly out of focus
short: A ghostly translucent memory scene projected into the air by a small ember

name: Fall Rescue
desc: a small ember streaking down through dark cloud after a falling figure, a ribbon of warm gold light unfurling from it and wrapping around the figure, then lifting it back up toward a ledge in a long arc of sparks; soft, caring, not violent
short: A small ember streaking down through dark cloud after a falling figure

name: Leech Swarm
desc: a mass of Ember Leeches crawling over a stone bridge, chains and rock in a dense creeping carpet, glossy dark bodies with orange glowing rear sacs, dozens climbing over each other, some dropping off the edge into cloud, some clinging to a boot and rising up a leg, glowing sparks falling from their tails; uncomfortable, crawling, never gory
short: A mass of Ember Leeches crawling over a stone bridge

name: Dragon Roar and Flame
desc: a distant giant dragon's roar made visible: a huge pale shockwave ring expanding across a golden sky, scattering birds and tearing dust off nearby rock, a long jet of orange fire streaming across the sky behind it, embers raining, the underside of the clouds lit orange; far away and awesome, not attacking anyone
short: A distant giant dragon's roar made visible: a huge pale shockwave ring expanding

name: Mind-Vision Realm
desc: a dreamlike inner world seen when the eyes are closed: a black glassy plain like a still lake reflecting warm amber light, no horizon, drifting gold motes and thin lines of light, shapes appearing as soft glowing silhouettes, the edges of everything slightly blurred, deep calm; not a nightmare, a quiet theater of the mind
short: A dreamlike inner world seen when the eyes are closed: a black glassy plain like

name: Creator's Light
desc: a figure's open hands shaping living fire into a form: a bird made of gold-white flame lifting out of cupped palms, thin threads of light trailing from the fingertips, sparks turning into a flock of small light birds, soft warm glow on the hands and face; creation and beauty, calm and joyful
short: A figure's open hands shaping living fire into a form: a bird made of gold-white

name: The Mother
desc: the Mother, a woman in her thirties, calm and kind, dark hair tied back with a thin gold thread, a plain dark-brown wrap dress with a bronze clasp and a long scarf, bare forearms, gentle steady eyes that look slightly upward like someone always watching the sky; shown as a reference of her younger self (and a second small figure beside her at the same scale showing her older self at fifty: grey in her hair, thinner, tired, still kind) All people of Igara are fair-skinned and European-looking (varied chestnut, brown, dark-blond and grey hair, blue, grey, green and hazel eyes), dressed in clean simple well-made clothes with bare heads and hair visible, scarves only loosely around the neck. The underside is a ragged forest of long rock spires and hanging roots of very different lengths. OTHER WORLDS: Igara is not alone. A thick permanent bank of cloud is caught against the high peak and ridge; it rains and snow-melts there, feeding a crater lake near the summit. Great roots and vines grip the cliff edges and hang down the sides, and the greenest ground follows the water. grp: Day 1 · Stage 3: the Arena, sunset and the first night
narr: Narrator: "I slept under two moons, in a broken world, and for the first time in twelve years I did not dream of falling."
happens: The first night. Wide shot: two moons, three faint sky bars, the half-open Eye as a dull amber lamp, the dormant ring a closed ellipse of dark ember, and one tiny fire with a tiny figure asleep beside it. Day 1 ends. Sleep takes the whole realm in one frame. Where he sleeps: in a shallow rock hollow on the arena island's edge, curled on his cape on warm stone, scarf as a pillow, the bow within reach. Who is beside him: nobody; Pip sleeps in his palm and the dim Cinder floats by his head. Warmth comes from the glowing cracks and a small fire. Light: three faint sky bars, the half-open Eye like a dull lamp, two moons. He is alone, and that is the point.

name: Sacred Arc
desc: a tall recurve bow of pale sky-ash wood with thin bronze inlay along the limbs, a leather-wrapped grip, a faint orange ember line down the inner curve, a braided string
short: His bow: plain wood, bronze inlay
note: Gets: Given on Island 1 (first real pickup). Use: Draws, aims, fires every arrow type. Never on fire itself. Book: Felicia: weapons. Swink: one tool, many meanings. WHAT IT DOES: Draws, aims and fires every arrow. Never burns itself. Its string hums one low note tuned to the Eye. FUN WAYS TO PLAY: Pluck the string idle: it plays the note, and nearby lanterns answer with a glow. · Hold the draw longer and the inlay warms, then a held breath steadies the aim. · Tap the limb on stone: a hollow knock tells you if the rock behind is solid or hollow. SOUND EFFECTS: Pickup: deep wood groan. Draw: creak rising in pitch. Release: one low thrum. Idle: faint string hum. Fail: dry slack twang.
